title: Glossary
markdown:
Every term from the course, in alphabetical order. The lesson that introduces each one is in brackets.

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Abstract class** | A class that cannot be created with `new`; it shares code and declares members that derived classes must implement. (3.03) |
| **Access modifier** | `public`, `private`, `protected` or `internal`: who may use a member or type. (3.01) |
| **Assembly** | The `.dll` or executable a project compiles into. (6.01) |
| **async / await** | Marks a method that can pause at `await` until a task finishes, without blocking a thread. (5.01) |
| **Attribute** | Information attached to code in square brackets, such as `[Fact]`, read with reflection. (6.02) |
| **Auto-property** | A property whose hidden field the compiler creates: `public string Name { get; set; }`. (3.01) |
| **Base class** | The class another class derives from. (3.03) |
| **Binding** | A link in XAML between a control and a view-model property. (6.04) |
| **Boxing** | Wrapping a value type in an object, which happens when it is stored as `object`. (4.01) |
| **CancellationToken** | A token passed to long operations so the caller can ask them to stop. (5.02) |
| **Class** | A reference type describing objects: their data and behaviour. (3.01) |
| **Class library** | A project that builds a `.dll` for other projects to use. (6.01) |
| **Closure** | A lambda together with the outer variables it captures. (4.02) |
| **Collection expression** | `[1, 2, 3]`: one syntax to create arrays, lists and spans. (2.02) |
| **Composition root** | The one place where an application's objects are created and connected. (6.03) |
| **Constraint** | `where T : ...`: a requirement on a generic type parameter. (4.01) |
| **Constructor** | The method that runs when an object is created with `new`. (3.01) |
| **Deferred execution** | A LINQ query or iterator doing its work only when enumerated. (2.04) |
| **Delegate** | A type for references to methods; `Func` and `Action` are the common ones. (4.02) |
| **Dependency injection** | Giving a class the services it needs through its constructor. (6.03) |
| **Dictionary** | A collection of key-value pairs with fast lookup by key. (2.03) |
| **Dispose** | The method of `IDisposable` that releases a resource such as a file. (4.04) |
| **Encapsulation** | Keeping data private and exposing only safe operations on it. (3.01) |
| **Event** | A member that notifies subscribers that something happened; `+=` subscribes. (4.02) |
| **Exception** | An object thrown to signal an error, caught with `try`/`catch`. (4.03) |
| **Exception filter** | `catch (E e) when (condition)`: catch only some exceptions of a type. (4.03) |
| **Extension method** | A static method usable as if it were a method of another type, marked with `this` on its first parameter. (3.05) |
| **Garbage collector** | The part of .NET that frees memory no longer referenced. (4.04) |
| **Generic** | A type or method with type parameters, such as `List<T>`. (4.01) |
| **HashSet** | A collection of unique values with fast `Contains`. (2.03) |
| **HttpClient** | The class that sends HTTP requests; created once and reused. (5.05) |
| **IEnumerable<T>** | The interface of everything that can be looped over with `foreach`. (4.05) |
| **Immutable** | Cannot be changed after creation, like strings and records. (1.04) |
| **Inheritance** | A class taking the members of a base class and extending them. (3.03) |
| **init** | A property accessor that allows setting only while the object is created. (3.01) |
| **Interface** | A contract of members that implementing types must provide. (3.04) |
| **Interpolated string** | `$"Hello {name}"`: a string with values inserted, optionally formatted. (1.04) |
| **Iterator** | A method using `yield return` to produce a sequence lazily. (4.05) |
| **JSON** | A text format for data, read and written with `System.Text.Json`. (5.04) |
| **Lambda** | An inline anonymous function: `x => x * 2`. (2.04) |
| **LINQ** | Query methods such as `Where`, `Select` and `GroupBy` on any sequence. (2.04) |
| **List<T>** | A growable array. (2.02) |
| **Local function** | A method declared inside another method or in top-level statements. (2.01) |
| **lock** | A statement that lets only one thread at a time run a block. (5.02) |
| **MVVM** | Model-View-ViewModel: the UI pattern that keeps screen logic in a testable view model. (6.04) |
| **Namespace** | A named group of types: `System.Collections.Generic`. (3.05) |
| **NuGet** | .NET's package manager. (6.01) |
| **Nullable reference types** | The feature that makes `string?` mean "may be null" and warns about unchecked uses. (2.05) |
| **Nullable value type** | `int?`: a value type that can also be null. (2.05) |
| **Object initializer** | `new Product { Name = "Tea" }`: setting properties when creating an object. (3.01) |
| **out parameter** | A parameter the method must assign, used for extra results. (2.01) |
| **Overloading** | Several methods with the same name and different parameters. (2.01) |
| **override** | Replacing a base class's virtual or abstract member in a derived class. (3.03) |
| **Pattern matching** | Testing a value's type, shape or range with `is` and `switch`. (2.05) |
| **Polymorphism** | Calls on a base type running the version of the actual object's class. (3.03) |
| **Primary constructor** | Constructor parameters written after the type name: `class Temperature(double c)`. (3.01) |
| **Property** | A member that looks like a field but runs `get` and `set` code. (3.01) |
| **Record** | A type with value equality, `with` copies and generated members, made for data. (3.02) |
| **ref parameter** | A parameter that passes the caller's variable itself. (2.01) |
| **Reference type** | A type whose variables hold references to objects: classes, strings, arrays. (1.02) |
| **Reflection** | Inspecting types, methods and attributes at run time, and calling them. (6.02) |
| **Solution** | A file grouping several projects. (6.01) |
| **static** | Belonging to the type itself rather than to an instance. (3.05) |
| **StringBuilder** | A mutable buffer for building strings efficiently. (1.04) |
| **Struct** | A value type, copied on assignment. (3.02) |
| **Switch expression** | `x switch { pattern => value, ... }`: a switch that produces a value. (1.05) |
| **Task** | An operation in progress; `Task<T>` produces a `T`. (5.01) |
| **Top-level statements** | Code written directly in `Program.cs`, wrapped in `Main` by the compiler. (1.01) |
| **Tuple** | A light group of values: `(string Name, int Age)`. (2.05) |
| **Type inference** | The compiler working out a type, as with `var` and generic arguments. (1.02) |
| **Unit test** | Code that checks a small part of a program automatically. (6.02) |
| **using** | Disposes an object at the end of a block (also: imports a namespace). (4.04) |
| **Value equality** | Two objects being equal when their data is equal, as for records. (3.02) |
| **Value type** | A type whose variables hold the data itself: numbers, bool, char, structs. (1.02) |
| **var** | Declares a local variable whose type the compiler infers. (1.02) |
| **virtual** | Marks a member that derived classes may override. (3.03) |
| **with expression** | Makes a copy of a record with some properties changed. (3.02) |
| **XAML** | The markup language that describes WPF, WinUI, Avalonia and MAUI windows. (6.04) |
| **yield return** | Hands out the next value of an iterator and pauses. (4.05) |
